author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Build a performance profile without unsafe speed-hack stacking
summary: Find the real bottleneck, change one control per test, separate global and per-game settings, and preserve a reversible Safe baseline instead of piling hacks together.
heroAlt: PCSX2 on-screen performance counters over a running game

blocks.text: Optimization begins with a reproducible limit

PS2 emulation can be limited by EE/VU emulation, GS rendering, shader compilation, storage stalls or thermal clocks. Multiple speed hacks may raise a counter while breaking timing, physics or audio, and they hide which subsystem mattered. A useful profile is a short record of one game's verified exceptions from Safe defaults.
Start from Optimal / Safe, native resolution and the system GPU driver. Do not combine cycle-rate, cycle-skip, frame-skip and graphics reductions in the same test.

Choose a demanding scene that can be replayed from an in-game save, not a save state created under unknown settings. Let the device cool, close background recording and fix brightness. Record emulation speed, CPU/GPU timing, audio behaviour and temperature trend for at least five minutes.

items: Safe profile and reset per-game overrides.
Repeatable in-game save and test route.
Renderer known to be correct.
Fixed brightness, orientation and power mode.
A simple results table with one row per change.

blocks.text: Isolate the bottleneck before applying an exception

items: 1. Measure the Safe baseline at native resolution. Lower resolution one step; if speed does not change, graphics load is probably not the primary limit.
2. Restore resolution and compare renderer paths only if visual correctness permits.
3. When CPU timing is the limit, test the least aggressive documented performance option once; replay the route and inspect game logic and audio.
4. Reject any setting that creates intermittent speed, physics errors, missing effects or save instability even when average FPS rises.
5. Save only the winning change in the game's profile and retest a separate title to confirm global settings stayed untouched.

blocks.text: The profile passes when the full route remains correct and smoother across three runs, including a warm run. Emulation speed and frame pacing matter more than a peak FPS number. Audio pitch, scripted events, collision and menus are timing checks; if any diverge, the speed gain is not valid.

items: One documented override explains the improvement.
Warm-session speed remains within the target range.
Audio, physics and scripted sequences behave normally.
Save/load and memory-card writes still work.
Other games retain the Safe global profile.

blocks.text: Reset the per-game profile first, then verify the Safe baseline before removing caches or reinstalling. If several undocumented changes already exist, take screenshots for reference, reset all advanced CPU/GS settings and rebuild one variable at a time. Preserve memory cards and in-game saves outside the reset scope.

items: Reset the affected game profile.
Restore native resolution and system driver.
Disable cycle changes and frame skipping.
Repeat the original baseline route before trying a different single change.
FPS rises but game runs too fast or slow: timing was traded for the counter.
Short test passes, warm run fails: thermal limit was ignored.
Resolution changes nothing: CPU rather than GPU is limiting.
Several hacks appear necessary: baseline is contaminated or the device cannot sustain the game.

blocks.text: Some titles will remain beyond a device's sustained capacity. A profile that admits that limit is safer than one that corrupts timing to appear playable. Keep the smallest stable exception, document the scene and revisit only after core, Android or driver changes provide a new baseline.
